_README: Example eval sweep (model bake-off) campaign. Copy, edit, and run:
npm run eval:sweep -- --config app/eval/sweep/sweep.config.example.json
THE CREDENTIAL DOES NOT BELONG IN THIS FILE, EVER.
AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK comes from the environment (see .env.example) and is read
only by app/agent/model-router/env-secret-manager.ts. There is no config field that
can hold it, and a config file gets committed, pasted, and attached to reports.
COST: this runs real paid model calls. arms x problems x sampleCount sessions. With
the settings below that is 2 arms x 46 problems x 5 samples = 460 sessions. Start with
a problems.ids selection of two or three designs and sampleCount 1 to smoke it, then
scale up. Cost is recorded, not limited, on purpose (see kill-switch.ts).
POSITIVE CONTROL: after each sample, the testbench our agent wrote is run against
RTLLM's own reference design. If the known-good design FAILS our testbench, that
testbench is not a measuring stick, so the sample is excluded from the pass@k
denominator and reported as instrument-invalid instead of as a model failure. It is a
deterministic toolchain run: no model call, no tokens, no session budget, no extra
sample or iteration, so it cannot move a measured number. It DOES cost wall clock -
one extra compile plus one simulation per sample, on the order of a second each on a
provisioned host, against tens of seconds of model time - so budget for it in
killSwitch.maxWallClockMs. It cannot be turned off: a pass@k whose instrument was
never validated is exactly the number this campaign exists to stop producing.
RESUME: re-running with the SAME config skips samples already in results.jsonl. Change
any field that can move a measured number and the config hash changes, so nothing is
reused - which is correct, because it is then a different experiment. The one exception
is captureArtifacts (see below): it writes diagnostic files and measures nothing, so it
is excluded from the hash and toggling it never invalidates a recorded sample.
_arms: Each arm is one point in the bake-off. Use "model" for one id across every role, or
"roleModels" to permute per role (generation, repair, orchestration, teaching,
hard-planning). Model ids are NOT validated against a catalog - the upstream catalog
moves - so a typo shows up as that arm failing, which is visible in the summary.
Reachable ids on this host are listed in app/eval/sweep/model-catalog.ts.
_problems: { "kind": "all" } runs the 46 scored RTLLM designs (50 imported, 48 build, 46 pass
their own golden testbench under Icarus). Or select a shard:
_sampling: sampleCount is the n in pass@k; ks are the k values reported. seed makes the run as
repeatable as a hosted provider allows - it is a hint to the endpoint, not a guarantee,
which is exactly why k samples are drawn instead of one.
_caps: The SAME student-session caps a real student gets. Every sample runs under these; the
sweep never widens them. maxIterations bounds the repair loop, so a never-passing
sample terminates instead of burning the night.
_limits: Sandbox resource limits for every iverilog/vvp run, including the golden judge and the
_costEnvelopeCents: The pennies-per-session envelope the harness asserts for every sample. A breach is
_prices: OPTIONAL, and it buys exactly one thing: the DOLLAR restatement of what was already
measured. The primary efficiency figures - tokens per verified artifact and wall clock
per verified artifact - are reported for every campaign whether this table is empty or
not, because the endpoint returns usage.prompt_tokens / usage.completion_tokens and the
runner observes the clock. No endpoint returns money, so cents only exist once you
A model with no entry has an UNKNOWN price - not a free one - so its arm reports the
dollar cost UNKNOWN and no dollar cost per verified artifact, rather than a misleading 0.
Left EMPTY on purpose: a vendor rate card goes stale and a stale number cited as measured
spend is worse than no number. Rates are cents per MILLION tokens; fill them from the
provider's current price list, and only if you intend to cite dollars.
_outputDir: Relative to the repository root. Holds manifest.json, results.jsonl (append-only),
summary.txt, and (when captureArtifacts is on) artifacts/. Gitignored: results are run
_captureArtifacts: Writes each sample's evidence to artifacts/<arm>/<problem>/sample-<n>/: the candidate
RTL, OUR generated testbench, the per-check verdicts, the simulator output, the failing
case, and the golden judge's verdict. ON by default, because the record alone cannot say
WHY our testbench and the independent judge disagreed - and without that, prompt and
model tuning is guesswork. Every field is capped, so a runaway model costs a truncated
file (marked as such) and never the run. Excluded from the config hash: it measures
nothing, so toggling it must not invalidate samples already paid for.
_concurrency: Samples in flight at once, across all arms. Conservative by default because the host
rate-limits before it refuses. Raise it if 429s stay rare; the backoff and the breaker
_transportRetry: TRANSPORT-level retry only: the same HTTP bytes resent when the wire or the provider
failed to answer (429 / 5xx / socket error). It is NEVER a second sampling attempt -
that would inflate pass@k. See app/eval/sweep/transport-retry.ts. The breaker turns a
sustained outage into a clean stop instead of a matrix full of failures.
_killSwitch: Stops DISPATCH at a sample boundary, so in-flight samples finish and everything already
completed stays on disk and resumable. Cost is deliberately not a limiter.
